citations.review_text: A fantastic collection of campaigns and multiplayer. I would start here if you are a new Halo fan instead of Campaign Evolved. The ability to toggle between new and old graphics at the press of a button is a great idea and is well implemented. Plenty of legacy options to choose from as well like having a lowered crosshair is also a welcome addition.

$50 for a slopified remake vs $40 ($10 when on sale) for a collection that includes all the Bungie made/pre 343 Halo games (both original and anniversary editions of CE and 2), and modding support for all 6 games.

Go figure.

Do not buy 2026 Campain Evolved. BUY THIS!!!

You get 6 Halo games!!! Play the older games with the classic or new remade "anniversary" graphics. No ultra woke nonsense. All brilliant games, this collection is insane value especially when on sale.

The things I like about Halo1:

So far Halo 1 is fun, you can press TAB to switch from the new graphics to the old one.


The things I don't like about Halo1:

I was having trouble with the stage I'm at in Halo1, so I just wanted to reload my save point to restart instead of dying so I pressed "Restart" and the game restarted the whole level because I pressed "Restart".

The only other option was "Last checkpoint" which is not what I want either lol 

I don't like the way vehicules are driven. I get it, it was on Xbox and you needed a system that is fool proof, well it's not. It's the most anoying thing ever.

This is the definitive way to play Halo. Halo Master Chief collection offers nearly every single Halo experience from Reach all the way to Halo 4, allowing you to play through multiple campaigns, multiplayers etc. The insane amount of achievements spread across all campaigns and multiplayers leaves plenty to go for. Multiple difficulties for every campaign allows you to challenge yourself depending on what your looking for.

The Halo Campaign Evolved anniversary edition even allows you to switch between the original graphics settings and the new remastered settings on the fly by simply pressing TAB. It's awesome

Overall if you are even remotely a fan of halo, or are looking for a way to jump in and enjoy the story in order then there is no better way than this collection. If you ever find it on sale, its a instant buy. 

Thanks for reading.

If you grew up playing Halo, this collection is a perfect throwback that feels just right. If you didn't, it's still one of the best ways to experience one of gaming's most influential first-person shooter series.

Six games, lots of exciting missions you'll remember, amazing music, and multiplayer that still works really well today. The option to switch between original and enhanced graphics in Halo: Combat Evolved and Halo 2 isn't just a fun feature—it's an interesting way to see how much game development has advanced over time. The campaigns are still the best part, with great scenes to remember, good co-op play, and a game that still feels fun to play even after many years.

That said, the collection isn't perfect. The PC release had some problems at first, but things are much better now.However, you might still come across some glitches, issues with matching players, or a UI that doesn't work consistently. Some games had more improvements than others, which made the whole experience feel a bit inconsistent.

It's still tough to complain when you're getting six legendary games all in one package. No matter if you're here for the campaigns, Forge, Firefight, or multiplayer, there's way too much content for the price.

Pros:

Six amazing Halo games all in one collection.
* Timeless campaigns with co-op support
Great value for the amount of content.
* Classic/remastered graphics toggle is brilliant
* Active enough multiplayer to enjoy

Cons:

* Occasional bugs and matchmaking issues
* UI can be clunky
Some titles are easier to keep in good condition than others.

Even though it has some issues, Halo: The Master Chief Collection is a tribute to one of the biggest and best gaming series ever. It's not perfect, but if you like playing first-person shooter games, it's definitely worth having.

Recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the collection includes the ability to instantly switch back and forth between classic and remastered graphics during gameplay and cutscenes.

citations.review_text:
The BAD: Connectivity issues out the wazoo. Cosmetics are not great and are too abundant, often feeling "unearned". Obvious cheaters and aimbot's which is insane considering it claims MCC uses anti-cheats on launching. It is the opposite of optimized. It is BONKERS how much space this game takes up for what it is. Each of these games fit nearly entirely on a single disc. The sound for each game except Reach and 4 feel-compressed weird? Even when I turn the score way down and my system all the way up I can often barely hear the dialogue over the ambiance and music, I swapped between audio devices, nothing helped. The original games aren't like this, I have my original and 360 set up and they don't have this problem. It could just be my PC doing something I suppose but I don't know why Reach would be fine but CE and 2 have problems. 
 
The Nostalgia: I love Halo, I'm a big fan of the series.  Sadly though this version has almost NONE of the special content that made the Halo collectors editions special. I'd hate for all those cool behind the scenes and extra features to get lost to time. (Halo 2-"Another Day at the Beach) etc. Look it up, treat yourself to the secret intimacy of the world. 

The Good: Halo stands as a testament to an era of FPS often forgotten about with how fast past modern shooters can be. Each of the games plays slightly unique from the others while the basic premise and systems remains the same, even the controls vary between games. The story and environmental work is exceptional. I think it truly stands alone in terms of experience. I laugh, I cried, I fought until I didn't want to anymore. It's a GREAT series. Start to finish, some of the best gaming you can have. COOP is prime. Voice Acting, GOATED. Level Design: Prepare to get lost in the sauce. Just look up the cast list for Halo 3, it's so top tier.
 
Final 2 cents: If you've played Halo before and you're looking to return to the Multiplayer experience from 360 days, you're probably going to…

I’ve played a lot of games over the years, but few collections have genuinely impressed me the way Halo: The Master Chief Collection has. What stands out to me most is not just the amount of content included, but the care, scale, and legacy behind it. It feels less like a normal game collection and more like a complete preservation of one of the most important franchises in gaming history.

What immediately impressed me was the sheer scope of the experience. Having multiple Halo titles brought together in one place already feels ambitious, but the way MCC allows me to move through different generations of Halo seamlessly is what makes it exceptional. I can go from the atmosphere and mystery of Halo: Combat Evolved to the emotional weight of Halo Reach, then into the larger-scale battles of Halo 3, all without feeling disconnected. It genuinely feels like a journey through gaming history.

Another thing that impressed me deeply is how much effort went into modernization without destroying the original identity of the games. The updated visuals are incredible, especially when switching between classic and remastered graphics. That feature alone constantly reminds me how advanced these games were for their time. Instead of replacing the originals, MCC respects them. It allows me to appreciate both the nostalgia and the technical improvements at the same time.

The multiplayer experience is another major reason why I admire MCC so much. The amount of maps, modes, customization options, and cross-game playlists creates almost endless replay value. It feels like a celebration of everything Halo multiplayer has ever represented — competitive gameplay, teamwork, creativity, and unforgettable moments with other players. Few collections manage to preserve online communities the way MCC has.

I’m also impressed by how the developers continued improving the collection over time. MCC had a difficult launch historically, but what matters to me is the commitment shown afte…

Never was able to experience HALO on the xbox growing up as a kid so playing this and even being able to switch between classic graphics and remastered graphics was pretty cool! Generational game that has aged fairly well.

"Sir, Finishing This Fight." - Master Chief (Halo 2)

I originally played Halo 1 and Halo 2 solo years ago, but this time I experienced the entire collection in co-op with a friend. My review is based solely on the campaign.

The Anniversary editions of Halo: Combat Evolved and Halo 2 are incredible. Being able to press 'Tab' and instantly switch between the original and remastered graphics really puts into perspective how far game visuals have come. Halo 2's remastered cutscenes feel like a 'blockbuster movie', and I'm still a huge fan of dual-wielding weapons. Halo 3 is the complete package for me, with the perfect balance of story, gameplay, and unforgettable moments. Nothing beats jumping into a 'Scorpion Tank' and obliterating everything in your path. One moment you're battling the military-focused Covenant; the next, you're being hunted by an aggressive, parasitic hive mind. NEED FLOOD-THEMED WEAPONS LOL. ODST and Reach were fantastic spin-offs that offered unique perspectives and were genuinely enjoyable.

While Halo 4 was the newest game in the MCC, it wasn't for me. The story didn't feel engaging enough, gameplay felt repetitive, grunts lost their originality, energy weapons were less flashy, new race were ok (liked their new weapons though) and I found myself pushing through the missions just to reach the ending.

Overall, Halo MCC is absolutely worth your time. It's an outstanding collection that preserves the legacy of one of gaming's greatest franchises.

It's Halo 1-4 and Reach with better refresh rates; what's not to love? I totally forgot that they allow the graphics swapping during cutscenes. They also allow the graphics swapping in Halo 2 which is great. If you play the original halo with the classic graphics, it restores most of the original sounds which is one of the best parts. I am grateful x-box allows Steam users to play this game online without an Xbox live subscription and just an Xbox account sign in. I'm also grateful they listened to the fan base and added Halo Reach to the collection.  All these details makes the game 100% worth it if it's ever on sale for $10 again.

citations.review_text:
Halo has always been a nostalgic game for me. As i grew up with the franchise from 1 through Reach.

Sadly, the state of multiplayer games makes me wish i could refund the entire thing and wipe Halo clean out of my memory. Sure, you'll probably call it as "Skill Issue". But to me, it's these experiences within the game that set the memories to make the game what you love (or hate) about it.

Custom Game Browser's "Quick Search" will always find the same 1 game 14 times when there's 200 other lobbies going on (with open slots).

Here's why i despise multiplayer:
→ No button input response when pushing the action. For instance, I have Melee mapped to B. I go to melee the person in front of me who's 1 hit. As i've pushed it, they somehow manage to go through a full shield and insta-kill. Please tell me: how is that fair.
→ Griefing teammates. Just why do they have to exist. The point of a team game is "teamwork". Not killing off your team because you're a douche.
→ Badly constructed maps. I've played a huge variety of community made maps. While i'm not going to name specific maps, here's some things i can highlight about 1 map:
> Camping areas during Zombies with no way for the Zombies to even get close to the survivors.
→ Nobody else wants to test your custom made maps. Made a cool custom map. Nobody wants to join the lobby. Made a map using a safe area outside the map. Nobody wants to see it.
→ There is always a hardcore sweat on the enemy team. Dude, it's a casual game. Why so try hard?
→ Horrible map spawn points. CE takes the cake with this. Though i've had it happen in 3.

To sum it up: The game is only fair when the game is balanced and enjoyable. Not being spawn camped or being softlocked because there's no way to progress.

Shoutout to the mods of this game. Halo Kart, HaloWare, Cursed Vehicle Bus Test. They are amazing and enhance the game.

I'm sure there are other players, in my position who just want to have a fun time playing Halo. Not becoming depressive…

Halo is probably my favorite game of all time. Halo: CE, 2, 3, ODST, & Reach are the pinnacle of what make a great game that stands the test of time. Shout out to the modding community, they are the most passionate fans out there. Entire alternate campaigns add to the endless hours of raw unfiltered fun. Multiplayer is a blast and you can still find matches; if not, you can always resort to custom games browser. 

Pros: Halo, Halo 2, Halo 3, Halo ODST, Halo Reach. Timeless stories, great characters, unique sci-fi epic full of mystery and intrigue. Nearly limitless mods.

Cons: Halo 4. Original Loading Screens/Menus removed (not included). Takes forever to find a Big Team Battle Match for Halo 1&2 unless you play on the weekend (even then you'll be waiting some time).

P.S. 
Purple Cortana is best Cortana. 
Anyone who disagrees can, Sod Off!

claims.claim: Reviewers experience game crashes and matchmaking disconnects that result in temporary matchmaking bans.

citations.review_text: After the fumbles of 343 and microsoft I would stay away from these games. The community has turned toxic in multiplayer for some reason, due to the constant coddling of poor liberal values, poor matchmaking quality, and abuse of reporting in this game. The DCing from poor 3rd world host lobbies also ban you in matchmaking. Hopefully a studio one day can get the IP for Halo and do this story correctly. Insteading pushing Sierra 117 into a further black hole of incompetence.

Halo has always been a nostalgic game for me. As i grew up with the franchise from 1 through Reach.

Sadly, the state of multiplayer games makes me wish i could refund the entire thing and wipe Halo clean out of my memory. Sure, you'll probably call it as "Skill Issue". But to me, it's these experiences within the game that set the memories to make the game what you love (or hate) about it.

Custom Game Browser's "Quick Search" will always find the same 1 game 14 times when there's 200 other lobbies going on (with open slots).

Here's why i despise multiplayer:
→ No button input response when pushing the action. For instance, I have Melee mapped to B. I go to melee the person in front of me who's 1 hit. As i've pushed it, they somehow manage to go through a full shield and insta-kill. Please tell me: how is that fair.
→ Griefing teammates. Just why do they have to exist. The point of a team game is "teamwork". Not killing off your team because you're a douche.
→ Badly constructed maps. I've played a huge variety of community made maps. While i'm not going to name specific maps, here's some things i can highlight about 1 map:
> Camping areas during Zombies with no way for the Zombies to even get close to the survivors.
→ Nobody else wants to test your custom made maps. Made a cool custom map. Nobody wants to join the lobby. Made a map using a safe area outside the map. Nobody wants to see it.
→ There is always a hardcore sweat on the enemy team. Dude, it's a casual game. Why so try hard?
→ Horrible map spawn points. CE takes the cake with this. Though i've had it happen in 3.

To sum it up: The game is only fair when the game is balanced and enjoyable. Not being spawn camped or being softlocked because there's no way to progress.

Shoutout to the mods of this game. Halo Kart, HaloWare, Cursed Vehicle Bus Test. They are amazing and enhance the game.

I'm sure there are other players, in my position who just want to have a fun time playing Halo. Not becoming depressive…

The original games are amazing but the package they come in sucks. Still buggy after a decade of its original release. Custom lobbies barely function and you can expect temp bans from matchmaking when your game eventually crashes 😛

claims.claim: Reviewers cite hit registration issues in multiplayer, specifically identifying Halo and Halo 2 as the worst offenders.

citations.review_text: I suppose after 1100hrs and the better part of playing Halo for nearly 25 years, I should leave a review for Halo MCC. The core game is as close to the original as I'll probably see in my lifetime. I love it and will play it until my dying day. My only gripe, aside from obvious stuff like the matchmaking lobby, is the hit registration.  Halo and Halo 2 are the worst offenders here. I refuse to play Halo 1 MP because it's that bad. Halo 2 is pretty close. Overall you're crazy not to own this. When all the other FPS are doing slides, sprint, wall climbs etc,, Halo makes you take the damage like the terrible player that you are. Lastly, England and their teabags are what makes life worth living. If you love making tea, you'll love Halo MCC.

[h1] It's a good way to Play Halo [/h1]

MCC is for all of us that played the Original Bungie games from Halo Combat Evolved on the OG Xbox since 2001 all the way till Halo Reach in 2010 all of Bungies game still hold up... and then there's Halo 4.
There are many problems with MCC with some of the original Game engines not running like they did on launch day, Unbalanced Matches when doing PvP, Co-op Disconnections during games with friends or PvP, and many more that I am not aware of.

Unless you have an ORIGINAL XBOX from 2001 or a 360 to play the old Halo games this is unfortunately this will do, thankful it's not awful.

I am glad to still be able to play my childhood games and do these games with friends.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the collection includes multiple games, mod support, and a custom games browser, offering high overall value.

citations.review_text:
if you are new to the games, you are going to love them and you WILL be impressed with how much you get for the value. 
If you're like me and have been playing for 25 years, you will love the ability to marathon these games and do cross-game playlists. 
Oh and the multiplayer is still lit. 
It's Halo. This is like owning the Mona Lisa for $39.99
Halo 1/2/3/4/Reach in one package.  If you get it on one of the common sales for the collection, it's definitely worth picking up.  Multiplayer and mod support as well.

[h1] 10/10 - Amazing Franchise [/h1]

Halo has been very near and dear to me for over a decade, although I have 173 hours at the time of this review I have thousands on Xbox and on each of the originals. And from my experience with MCC I cannot stress how much I implore anyone reading this and considering Halo to get it. For a cheper price than entire triple A games today with common sales you can get 6 whole games with multiplayers and extra modes involved as well as moding capabilities from the workshop.

[h3] Story - 7.5/10 [/h3]
The story is quite good for an FPS game, it is no Telltale game levels of good or detailed but you will get attached to characters and be hooked to the plot with well written stories in each entry. Behind the hood is a lot of lore to get stuck into if you want with overall a very good story to guide you along.

[h3] Graphics - 7.5/10 [/h3]
The graphics of Halo is quite timeless in my opinion, however it would be foolish to say it wasn't getting a bit dated over 25 years. However, even in the oldest of them you can find beauty in the environments with great atmosphere and attention to detail despite the age of these games. From the dreamy snowy areas from Halo CE to the Jungles of Halo 3 or rainy night city in Halo 3 ODST, these game seriously hold up with visuals and atmosphere and graphics isn't much of a concern. This game is quite easy to run for most people due to the age of the games and you will mostly have no trouble playing at good frames (Halo 2 Anniversary is a ♥♥♥♥♥ to run on some levels). I do have to add, do not play Halo CE on the anniversary graphics, it fails to uphold what the original devs intended and is widely considered an absolute sin to play that way next to killing marines.

[h3] Music - 9/10 [/h3]
Nothing much to say here, the music made is iconic and extremely good with many people not even having played the game knowing some of them. It adds heavily to atmosphere or the level and are straight up absolute banger…

An absolute masterpiece of a collection and quite frankly, one of the greatest value propositions in all of PC gaming. This is the ultimate gaming time capsule in my opinon.

It’s no secret that the collection had a incredibly rough borderline shocking launch years ago. But the developers stuck with it and after years of meticulous updates and PC optimization with feature additions, the Master Chief Collection stands today as a flawless triumph ngl. You are getting six legendary games (usually at a quite frank steal when on sale), fully remastered with cross-play, Forge, and a unified multiplayer ecosystem for less than the price of a single modern AAA title.

Here is how the legendary saga breaks down:

>>>The Games<<<
HALO: COMBAT EVOLVED ANNIVERSARY: The blueprint that changed the industry forever. The sense of isolation on the mysterious ring world, the brilliant enemy AI and that iconic orchestral score still hit just as hard today. The ability to swap between the classic graphics and the remastered visuals with a single button press is a brilliant touch even if the classic atmosphere remains unmatched.

HALO 2: ANNIVERSARY: This is the gold standard of what a remaster should be in my opinion; the rewritten cutscenes by Blur Studio are breathtakingly beautiful looking like a modern sci-fi film. Mechanically it introduces dual-wielding and splits the narrative between the Master Chief and the Arbiter, expanding the lore of the Covenant in a deeply engaging way.

HALO 3: The grand finale of the original trilogy and a masterclass in sandbox design. Every level feels like an epic sweeping battlefield. The gunplay, the vehicles and the environmental storytelling culminate in one of the most satisfying conclusions to a gaming trilogy ever conceived.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that split-screen is missing from the PC release.

citations.review_text: Love all these games. However not having splitscreen still after all this time is a major let down.

Played through the whole thing solo on Legendary to get myself ready for the next Halo. That's a lot of hours with a controller in my hands, and most of them were good ones. The campaigns still hold up. Legendary solo is still Legendary solo. No complaints about the games themselves.

My problem is with what this collection is supposed to be. It's called the Master Chief Collection, and the pitch has always been "every Halo in one place." Except it isn't. Halo 5 isn't here. Infinite isn't here. Halo Wars isn't here. I get that there are technical and licensing reasons, but I'd have paid for DLC to fold them in without thinking twice. Having to bounce between three storefronts and two launchers to play a series that ships as a single package is exactly the problem this collection was made to solve.

Then there's the unlocks. There used to be cosmetics you earned by finishing every campaign on Legendary — a genuine badge, the kind of thing you'd only have if you'd actually put in the work. They patched that. Now you can just buy them. I found this out after the fact, which somehow made it worse. If the reward for the hardest thing in the game is also sitting in a storefront, the achievement stops meaning anything. It doesn't break the game, but it takes the air out of a playthrough I specifically undertook to earn something.

So: the games are great, the collection is fine, and the stewardship is disappointing. Buy it on sale, play the campaigns, don't expect the definitive Halo package the name promises.
